newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt mulls issuing privatisation bonds-paper.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt mulls issuing privatisation bonds-paper.

text.p: Italy's government is considering issuing privatisation bonds to taxpayers to offset the impact of an extraordinary 11.5 trillion lire ($7.6 billion) "Eurotax" included in the 1997 budget, an Italian newspaper reported.
Financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore said on Saturday that some seven trillion lire of the planned Eurotax would take the form of a once-off increase in income tax to be levied in 1997.

The Eurotax is part of a budget package of 62.5 trillion lire in deficit-cutting measures which the government hopes will smooth Italy's path towards founder membership of European economic and monetary union (EMU) in 1999.
The package was approved by the lower house of parliament on Saturday and now passes to the upper house (Senate) for ratification.

Details of the Eurotax have not yet been unveiled but the government is studying a plan to grant taxpayers, in return for payment of the income tax surcharge, bonds which would be convertible into shares in state companies earmarked for privatisation, Il Sole said.

However, if the EU Commission in Brussels were to object to the privatisation bond idea, the government would consider granting taxpayers special tax deductions in 1998 to compensate for the Eurotax, the newspaper said.
The balance of the Eutotax -- some 4.5 to five trillion lire -- will be raised by increased taxes on luxury goods, employee fringe benefits and a further crackdown on tax evasion, it added.
The plans are due to be spelt out a meeting between the government and trade union leaders on Monday.
